messages.subject: Hierarchical Finite Mixture Models
parts:
I have data comprised of 1,000 time observations across ~150 locations, and I'd like to estimate intercepts for each location. The data appear bi-modal and log-normal:


I believe a finite mixture model would be appropriate in this case. I followed along with Jim Savage's blog post here, but I'm not sure how to go from the mixture parameter estimation to the HLM intercepts. My raw data is attached, and the Stan mixture code I've been using is below. Any guidance would be appreciated.

// saved as finite_mixture_linear_regression.stan
data {
  int N;
  vector[N] y;
  int n_groups;
}
parameters {
  ordered[n_groups] mu;
  vector<lower = 0>[n_groups] sigma;
  simplex[n_groups] Theta;
}
model {
  vector[n_groups] contributions;
  // priors
  mu ~ normal(0, 10);
  sigma ~ cauchy(0, 3);
  Theta ~ dirichlet(rep_vector(2.0, n_groups));
  
  
  // likelihood
  for(i in 1:N) {
    for(k in 1:n_groups) {
      contributions[k] = log(Theta[k]) + normal_lpdf(y[i] | mu[k], sigma[k]);
    }
    target += log_sum_exp(contributions);
  }
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Hierarchical Finite Mixture Models
parts:
Not sure what you're asking. Is y already log transformed? If
not, you want to use lognormal_lpdf in the mixtures. mu are
your intercepts, so I'm not sure what you'rea sking here.

It'll be a bit more efficient if you just do the log once:

vector[n_groups] log_theta = log(Theta);

and then use log_theta[k] rather than log(Theta[k]).

You an also move the rep_vector into transformed data so you can
create it just once.

transformed data {
vector<lower=0>[n_groups] alpha = rep_vector(2, n_groups);
}

and then just use alpha.

- Bob
